question: Which of the following musical forms in Carnatic Classical is the simplest composition of raga?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gitam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gitam (Geetham) is the simplest and most elementary composition taught to a beginner in Carnatic classical music. (गीतम — कर्नाटक संगीत की सरलतम रचना)

 

• It is a short, simple melodic piece set to a single raga and tala, sung in one speed (madhyama kala), with no elaborate ornamentation — it is the first stage of the graded Carnatic pedagogy that follows Sarali Varisai, Janta Varisai and other exercises.

 

• Gitams are typically composed in praise of a deity or a guru and are meant to teach the student the basic outline (dhatu) of a raga before moving to more complex forms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The traditional graded order of learning in Carnatic music is: Sarali Varisai → Jantai Varisai → Alankaras → Gitam → Swarajati → Varnam → Kriti.

 

• Purandara Dasa, the 'Pitamaha (father) of Carnatic music', is credited with systematising this graded teaching method, including the Gitams.

 

NOTE

 

• Varnam (Option 1): A more advanced, technically demanding composition that showcases the full grammar of a raga; it is learnt after Gitams, not before.

 

• Pada (Option 2): A devotional/erotic-devotional (Sringara-bhakti) composition, usually in Telugu, that is musically and literarily more elaborate than a Gitam.

 

• Kirtnam (Kriti) (Option 4): The most developed and widely performed Carnatic composition form, with Pallavi, Anupallavi and Charanam sections — far more complex than a Gitam.

question: How can you insert a blank row at the top of a worksheet?
option_1: Right-click on the row number and select Insert.
option_2: Drag the mouse on the row border to select the row and click Insert in the Cells group on the Home tab.
option_3: Click on the row number and press the Insert key on the keyboard.
option_4: Click on the row number and press the Delete key on the keyboard.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right-click on the row number and select Insert.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Microsoft Excel, the standard way to insert a blank row at the top of a worksheet is to right-click the row number/header (e.g., row 1) and choose "Insert" from the context menu — this shifts the existing row (and everything below it) down by one row. (एक्सेल में पंक्ति जोड़ना — राइट-क्लिक करके इन्सर्ट चुनें)

 

• This can also be done via the Home tab → Cells group → Insert → Insert Sheet Rows after selecting the target row.

 

• A new row is always inserted above the selected row, which is why selecting row 1 and inserting places the new blank row at the very top.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Plus (+) also inserts a row (or column/cell, depending on selection) in Excel once a full row is selected.

 

• To insert multiple rows at once, select that many row headers before right-clicking and choosing Insert.

 

NOTE

 

• Drag the mouse on the row border... (Option 2): Dragging a row's border resizes the row's height; it does not select or insert a row.

 

• Click the row number and press Insert key (Option 3): The keyboard's Insert key has no such row-insertion function in Excel.

 

• Click the row number and press Delete key (Option 4): This deletes the row's contents (or the row itself, depending on selection), the opposite of inserting one.

question: In Microsoft PowerPoint, what is the shortcut key combination to insert a new slide in a presentation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ctrl + M.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Microsoft PowerPoint, the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + M inserts a new slide immediately after the currently selected slide. (नई स्लाइड जोड़ना — Ctrl + M)

 

• The new slide typically takes the same layout as the previous slide, and can be changed afterwards from the Home → Slides → Layout menu.

 

• This shortcut works both in the Normal view and in the Slide/Outline pane.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ctrl + D in PowerPoint duplicates the currently selected slide (or object), rather than inserting a fresh blank one.

 

• Other useful PowerPoint shortcuts: F5 starts the slideshow from the beginning, Shift + F5 starts it from the current slide, and Ctrl + N is used to open a new presentation file (as in most Office apps).

 

NOTE

 

• Ctrl + N (Option 1): Opens a new blank presentation, not a new slide within the current one.

 

• Ctrl + D (Option 2): Duplicates the selected slide/object rather than creating a fresh new slide.

 

• Ctrl + I (Option 3): This is the standard shortcut for Italic formatting of selected text, not slide insertion.

question: Which of the following was a feature of the Indian economy before the British rule?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Independent economy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Before the advent of British rule, the Indian economy was largely independent and self-contained, resting on a strong base of agriculture and world-famous handicrafts (cotton and silk textiles, metalwork, etc.). (स्वतंत्र अर्थव्यवस्था — ब्रिटिश शासन-पूर्व भारत)

 

• India was a major exporter of fine cotton and silk fabrics, spices, and other manufactured goods to Europe and Asia, and its village-based economy met most of its own needs without dependence on colonial trade structures.

 

• With the establishment of British colonial rule, this changed fundamentally — India was converted into a supplier of raw materials and a market for British manufactured goods, making its economy dependent on and subordinate to British economic interests (a classic pattern of colonial exploitation).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The decline of Indian handicrafts under British rule, caused by competition from machine-made British goods and discriminatory tariff policies, is often called the process of 'deindustrialisation'.

 

• Economic historians estimate that India's share of world manufacturing output fell drastically during the colonial period, even as it remained a leading textile exporter before British rule.

 

NOTE

 

• Prosperous economy (Option 1): While parts of the pre-British economy were flourishing, 'prosperous' does not capture the specific structural feature being tested here — the key point is the economy's self-contained, non-colonial independence.

 

• Self-reliant economy (Option 2): Close in spirit, but this is not the term used in the standard characterisation of the pre-British Indian economy for this question; the accepted descriptor is 'independent'.

 

• Dependent economy (Option 3): This describes the economy after, not before, British rule was established — colonialism is precisely what made the Indian economy dependent.

question:
A distinctive cross-shaped constellation best seen in the northern hemisphere during the summer and fall months around

September is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cygnus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cygnus, the Swan, is a prominent northern-hemisphere constellation whose brightest stars form a distinctive cross shape, earning it the popular name the 'Northern Cross'. (सिग्नस तारामंडल — उत्तरी क्रॉस)

 

• It is best viewed during the summer and early autumn months (around September) in the northern hemisphere, high overhead in the evening sky.

 

• Its brightest star, Deneb, forms one point of the well-known 'Summer Triangle' along with Vega (in Lyra) and Altair (in Aquila).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cygnus lies along the Milky Way and contains the famous Cygnus X-1, one of the first strong candidates identified for a stellar-mass black hole.

 

• The constellation is also associated with the North America Nebula and the Veil Nebula.

 

NOTE

 

• Pegasus (Option 1): A large constellation representing a winged horse, recognisable by the 'Great Square of Pegasus', visible in autumn but not cross-shaped.

 

• Ursa Major (Option 2): Contains the 'Big Dipper' asterism, shaped like a ladle/plough, not a cross, and is circumpolar (visible year-round) from most northern latitudes.

 

• Cassiopeia (Option 3): Recognisable by its distinctive 'W' or 'M' shape, not a cross, and is best seen in autumn/winter.

question: Which of the following dynasties' genealogy was found in the Bijolia inscription?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chahamana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bijolia inscription (1170 CE), found at Bijolia in present-day Rajasthan, is a key epigraphic source for the genealogy of the Chahamana (Chauhan) dynasty, particularly the Shakambhari branch. (बिजोलिया अभिलेख — चाहमान/चौहान वंश)

 

• It was composed by the poet Lolaka and lists the succession of Chahamana rulers, providing crucial chronological information used to reconstruct the dynasty's history, including the ancestry leading up to Prithviraj Chauhan (Prithviraj III).

 

• The Chahamanas ruled from their capital at Ajmer/Shakambhari and were among the principal Rajput powers of north-western India in the 12th century.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important sources for Chahamana history include the Prithviraja Vijaya and Prithviraj Raso.

 

• The Chahamanas were eventually defeated by Muhammad of Ghor at the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 CE).

 

NOTE

 

• Gahadavala (Option 1): A dynasty that ruled over the Kannauj/Varanasi region; their history is known chiefly from copper-plate land-grant inscriptions, not the Bijolia inscription.

 

• Parmara (Option 2): Ruled over Malwa (capital Dhara/Ujjain); associated inscriptions include those from Udaipur and Dhar, not Bijolia.

 

• Chandela (Option 4): Ruled Bundelkhand (Khajuraho, Mahoba); their genealogy is chiefly known from inscriptions found at Khajuraho and Mahoba, not Bijolia.

question: In Kabaddi, a super tackle is when a raider is caught/self out/declared out with or less than how many defenders defending?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Three.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Kabaddi, a Super Tackle occurs when the defending team successfully tackles the raider (raider caught/self out/declared out) while having three or fewer defenders on the mat at the time of the tackle. (सुपर टैकल — कबड्डी)

 

• A Super Tackle rewards the defending team with 2 points instead of the usual 1, recognising the higher difficulty of tackling a raider with a depleted defence.

 

• This rule specifically encourages aggressive raiding against a weakened defence and adds a strategic, high-value scoring dimension to the game (used prominently in the Pro Kabaddi League).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A standard Kabaddi team fields 7 players on the mat at a time; the number of defenders can fall below 7 due to players already being 'out'.

 

• Other special scoring terms in Kabaddi include the 'All Out' (all opposition players out, earning 2 bonus points) and the 'Bonus Point' (raider crosses the bonus line without being tackled).

 

NOTE

 

• Four, Six, Five (Options 1, 3 and 4): The official Super Tackle threshold is fixed at three or fewer defenders, not four, five, or six — these options do not match the codified Kabaddi rule.

question: Bali Yatra, is a traditional cultural festival of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bali Yatra ('Voyage to Bali') is a major traditional festival of Odisha, held annually on the banks of the Mahanadi river at Cuttack, beginning on Kartik Purnima. (बालि यात्रा — ओडिशा)

 

• It commemorates the ancient maritime trade links between the Kalinga (Odisha) region and Southeast Asian islands like Bali, Java and Sumatra (Indonesia), when Odiya sailors (called 'Sadhabas') set sail to trade in textiles, spices and other goods.

 

• The festival features boat-shaped lamps floated on rivers ('Boita Bandana'), a large fair, and cultural performances, and is considered one of the largest open-air fairs in Asia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Odisha's other major festivals include the Rath Yatra of Puri and Konark Dance Festival near the Sun Temple.

 

• The Bali Yatra tradition is echoed by the modern 'Boita Bandana' ritual performed by devotees, symbolising the ancient voyages.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar (Option 2): Known for festivals such as Chhath Puja and Sonepur Cattle Fair, not Bali Yatra.

 

• West Bengal (Option 3): Known for Durga Puja, not Bali Yatra.

 

• Assam (Option 4): Known for the Bihu festival, not Bali Yatra.

question:
In April 2023, India's External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar launched the project for restoration of which of the following

ghats?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tulsi Ghat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In April 2023, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, during his visit to Kampala, Uganda, launched the 'Tulsi Ghat Restoration Project'. (तुलसी घाट पुनरुद्धार परियोजना — कंपाला, युगांडा)

 

• This Tulsi Ghat is located on the banks of Lake Victoria/River Nile area in Kampala, historically linked to the Indian community in Uganda, and the restoration was undertaken as part of India's outreach to its diaspora and cultural diplomacy efforts.

 

• The project reflects India's continuing engagement with Uganda and the wider East African Indian diaspora, reinforcing historical and cultural ties.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• S. Jaishankar's Uganda visit in April 2023 was part of broader outreach to African nations under India's 'Africa policy', aimed at strengthening trade, cultural and diaspora relations.

 

• Ghats along the Ganga at Varanasi — such as Manikarnika, Assi and Dashashwamedh — are separately covered under India's domestic Namami Gange and river-front redevelopment programmes.

 

NOTE

 

• Manikarnika Ghat (Option 1): A major cremation ghat at Varanasi, not the ghat referenced in this 2023 Uganda project.

 

• Assi Ghat (Option 2): A well-known ghat at Varanasi, unrelated to this project.

 

• Cheer Ghat (Option 3): Not the ghat associated with this restoration project; it does not match the actual 2023 announcement.

question:
In which year did Eric A. Cornell, Wolfgang Ketterle and Carl E. Wieman receive the Nobel Prize in Physics for the achieving

'Bose-Einstein condensation in dilute gases of alkali atoms'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2001.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Nobel Prize in Physics 2001 was awarded jointly to Eric A. Cornell, Wolfgang Ketterle and Carl E. Wieman 'for the achievement of Bose-Einstein condensation in dilute gases of alkali atoms, and for early fundamental studies of the properties of the condensates'. (बोस-आइंस्टीन संघनन — भौतिकी नोबेल 2001)

 

• Bose-Einstein Condensation (BEC) is a state of matter formed when a dilute gas of bosons is cooled to temperatures very close to absolute zero, causing a large fraction of the atoms to occupy the same lowest quantum state.

 

• The phenomenon was theoretically predicted by Satyendra Nath Bose and Albert Einstein in the 1920s, but was only experimentally achieved by Cornell and Wieman's team in 1995, with Ketterle achieving it independently soon after.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Satyendra Nath Bose's work on quantum statistics for photons (Bose statistics) laid the theoretical foundation for what Einstein later extended to atoms, giving BEC its name.

 

• BEC is sometimes called the 'fifth state of matter', alongside solid, liquid, gas and plasma.

 

NOTE

 

• 2002, 2000, 2003 (Options 1, 2 and 4): The Nobel Prize in Physics for Bose-Einstein condensation was awarded specifically in 2001, not in these other years.

question:
In which judgement did the Supreme Court extend the scope of Article 21 and observed that 'the Right to education flows

directly from the Right to life'?
option_1: Kharak Singh v State of UP
option_2: Malak Singh v State of Punjab
option_3: Mohini Jain v State of Karnataka
option_4: Neerja Choudhari v State of M. P.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohini Jain v State of Karnataka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka (1992), the Supreme Court of India held that the Right to Education is implicit in and flows directly from the Right to Life guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution. (शिक्षा का अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 21, मोहिनी जैन मामला)

 

• The Court ruled that every citizen has a right to education, and that this right, until effectively provided for, must be interpreted as encompassed by Article 21, since the right to life and dignity cannot be assured without it.

 

• This ruling was later reaffirmed and refined in Unni Krishnan, J.P. v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1993), which held the right to education is available up to the age of 14 as a fundamental right, and beyond that subject to the economic capacity of the state — this eventually led to the insertion of Article 21A by the 86th Constitutional Amendment (2002).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 21A, inserted by the 86th Amendment, makes free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14 years a fundamental right, operationalised through the Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009.

 

• Article 21 ('Protection of life and personal liberty') has been progressively interpreted by the judiciary to include a wide range of rights, such as the right to livelihood, clean environment, privacy, and education.

 

NOTE

 

• Kharak Singh v State of UP (Option 1): Dealt with police surveillance and the right to privacy under Article 21, not the right to education.

 

• Malak Singh v State of Punjab (Option 2): Concerned surveillance of history-sheeters and the right to privacy, not education.

 

• Neerja Choudhari v State of M.P. (Option 4): Related to the rehabilitation of bonded labourers under Article 21, not the right to education.

question: When did the first War of Indian Independence (Sepoy Mutiny) start?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1857.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The First War of Indian Independence, also known as the Sepoy Mutiny or the Revolt of 1857, began on 10 May 1857 at Meerut, when sepoys of the Bengal Army rose up in revolt. (1857 का विद्रोह — प्रथम स्वतंत्रता संग्राम)

 

• The immediate trigger was the introduction of the new Enfield rifle cartridges, rumoured to be greased with cow and pig fat, offending both Hindu and Muslim sepoys.

 

• The revolt spread quickly to Delhi, Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi and other parts of northern and central India, with leaders like Bahadur Shah Zafar, Rani Lakshmibai, Tantia Tope, Nana Saheb and Begum Hazrat Mahal playing key roles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The revolt led to the end of East India Company rule in India and the transfer of power to the British Crown via the Government of India Act, 1858.

 

• Historian V.D. Savarkar popularised the term 'The Indian War of Independence 1857' for this uprising in his 1909 book of the same name.

 

NOTE

 

• 1819, 1887, 1839 (Options 1, 2 and 4): None of these years mark the start of the 1857 uprising; the revolt is definitively dated to 1857.

question:
In a dihybrid cross between two heterozygous fruit flies with brown bodies and red eyes (BbEe X BbEe), what will be the

probability of getting BBEE genotype?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1/16.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a dihybrid cross between two individuals heterozygous for two independently assorting genes (BbEe × BbEe), each gene pair segregates independently as per Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment. (द्विसंकर क्रॉस — मेंडल का स्वतंत्र अपव्यूहन नियम)

 

• For a single gene cross Bb × Bb, the probability of getting the homozygous dominant genotype BB is 1/4.

 

• Similarly, for Ee × Ee, the probability of getting the homozygous dominant genotype EE is also 1/4.

 

• Since the two genes assort independently, the combined probability of getting BBEE is the product of the two individual probabilities: 1/4 × 1/4 = 1/16.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A full dihybrid cross (BbEe × BbEe) produces a 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation, corresponding to a 16-square Punnett grid.

 

• Of the 16 possible genotype combinations, only 1 combination corresponds to BBEE, confirming the 1/16 probability.

 

NOTE

 

• 1/4 (Option 2): This would be the probability of obtaining just one homozygous dominant trait (e.g., BB alone), not both BB and EE together.

 

• 1/8 (Option 3): Does not correspond to any standard probability outcome in this dihybrid cross for the BBEE combination.

 

• 1/2 (Option 4): This is the probability of a simple monohybrid heterozygous outcome (Bb or Ee) in a single-gene cross, not the BBEE genotype in a dihybrid cross.

question: Which of the following Articles was amended by The Constitution Fiftieth Amendment Act, 1984?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 33.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution (Fiftieth Amendment) Act, 1984, amended Article 33 of the Constitution. (संविधान 50वां संशोधन अधिनियम, 1984 — अनुच्छेद 33)

 

• Article 33 empowers Parliament to restrict or abrogate the fundamental rights of members of the armed forces, police forces, and forces maintaining public order, in order to ensure proper discharge of their duties and maintenance of discipline.

 

• The 50th Amendment extended this power to cover members of forces charged with the protection of property, and persons employed in bureaus or organisations engaged in intelligence, counter-intelligence, or in communication systems set up for the armed/police/security forces.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 33 is one of the exceptions carved out within Part III (Fundamental Rights) of the Constitution, alongside Articles 34 (martial law) and 31A/31B/31C (property and land reform-related restrictions).

 

• Such special provisions balance individual fundamental rights against the operational discipline needs of security and intelligence forces.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 56 (Option 1): Deals with the term of office of the President of India, unrelated to the 50th Amendment.

 

• Article 78 (Option 3): Relates to the duties of the Prime Minister with respect to furnishing information to the President.

 

• Article 99 (Option 4): Concerns the oath or affirmation by members of Parliament, unrelated to this amendment.

question: ___________ has called the Right to Constitutional Remedy as the 'Soul of the Constitution'.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr. BR Ambedkar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the chief architect of the Indian Constitution, famously described Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) as 'the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it'. (संविधान की आत्मा — डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर, अनुच्छेद 32)

 

• Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of fundamental rights, through writs such as Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo Warranto.

 

• Ambedkar considered this provision indispensable because without an effective remedy to enforce them, fundamental rights would be rendered meaningless — hence the description as the Constitution's 'soul'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dr. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly and is widely regarded as the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'.

 

• The Supreme Court under Article 32 and High Courts under Article 226 both have writ jurisdiction, though Article 226's scope is broader (covering fundamental as well as other legal rights).

 

NOTE

 

• Lal Lajpat Rai, Jawaharlal Nehru, Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Options 2, 3 and 4): These leaders made notable contributions to India's freedom struggle, but the specific description of Article 32 as the 'soul of the Constitution' is attributed to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, not to them.

question: Which type of soil is found on about 40% of the total area of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alluvial soil.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alluvial soil is the most widespread soil type in India, covering roughly 40% of the country's total land area, mainly across the Northern Plains (Indus-Ganga-Brahmaputra plains) and parts of the eastern coastal deltas. (जलोढ़ मिट्टी — भारत के लगभग 40% क्षेत्र में)

 

• It is formed by the deposition of silt carried by rivers originating in the Himalayas, making it extremely fertile and ideal for intensive agriculture, especially crops like rice, wheat, and sugarcane.

 

• Alluvial soil is typically classified into Bhangar (older alluvium) and Khadar (newer alluvium, found in flood plains).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Black soil (regur soil) covers about 15-16% of India's area, mainly over the Deccan Plateau, and is ideal for cotton cultivation.

 

• Red and Yellow soil covers roughly 18-19% of the area (parts of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Odisha, Chhattisgarh), while Laterite soil covers a smaller share, found in high rainfall areas like parts of Kerala, Karnataka and the North-East.

 

NOTE

 

• Black soil (Option 1): Covers a much smaller share (~15-16%) of India's area, concentrated in the Deccan trap region, not 40%.

 

• Red and Yellow soil (Option 2): Covers a smaller share (~18-19%) than alluvial soil.

 

• Laterite soil (Option 3): Covers the smallest share among these, restricted to specific high-rainfall regions, not 40% of the country.

question:
_____ at Market Price refers to the sum total of factor incomes earned by residents of a country during an accounting year

including net indirect taxes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Net National Product (NNP).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Net National Product (NNP) at Market Price is defined as the sum total of factor incomes (wages, rent, interest, profit) earned by the normal residents of a country during an accounting year, including net indirect taxes (indirect taxes minus subsidies). (शुद्ध राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद — बाजार मूल्य पर)

 

• NNP at Factor Cost (National Income) = sum of factor incomes earned by normal residents (without indirect taxes); adding net indirect taxes to this converts it to NNP at Market Price.

 

• NNP is derived from GNP by subtracting depreciation (consumption of fixed capital): NNP = GNP − Depreciation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• National Income (NI) in India is conventionally taken to mean NNP at Factor Cost.

 

• The relationship chain is: GDP → GNP (add net factor income from abroad) → NNP (subtract depreciation) → National Income (convert to factor cost).

 

NOTE

 

• Net Domestic Product (NDP) (Option 1): Measures income generated within the domestic territory only, excluding net factor income from abroad, and does not match this definition based on 'residents'.

 

• Gross Domestic Product (GDP) (Option 2): Is a gross measure (before depreciation) of output within the domestic territory, not specifically factor incomes of residents.

 

• Gross National Product (GNP) (Option 3): Is the gross measure (before subtracting depreciation) of income earned by residents, not the net measure described in the question.

question: According the Census of India 2011, which group of states has the least urban population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh and Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, Himachal Pradesh (about 10%) and Bihar (about 11.3%) recorded the lowest levels of urbanisation among Indian states, meaning the smallest proportion of their population lived in urban/urban-agglomeration areas. (न्यूनतम शहरी जनसंख्या — हिमाचल प्रदेश और बिहार)

 

• Both states have a predominantly rural, agriculture-based population, with only a small share residing in towns and cities as per the 2011 enumeration.

 

• In contrast, states/UTs with high urbanisation include Goa, Mizoram, Tamil Nadu and Union Territories like Delhi and Chandigarh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's overall urban population as per Census 2011 was about 31.16% of the total population.

 

• Bihar, despite being one of India's most populous states in absolute terms, remains one of the least urbanised due to its predominantly rural, agrarian economy.

 

NOTE

 

• Himachal Pradesh and Meghalaya (Option 1): Meghalaya's urbanisation level (about 20%) is considerably higher than Bihar's, so this pairing does not represent the least-urbanised group.

 

• Uttar Pradesh and Bihar (Option 3): Uttar Pradesh's urbanisation (about 22%) is higher than Himachal Pradesh's, so this is not the least-urbanised pairing.

 

• Madhya Pradesh and Bihar (Option 4): Madhya Pradesh's urbanisation (about 27-28%) is considerably higher than Himachal Pradesh's, so this pairing does not match the lowest group.

question:
________ was an Indian dancer and choreographer best known for creating a fusion style of dance adapting European

theatrical techniques to Indian classical and folk-dance forms.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uday Shankar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Uday Shankar was a pioneering Indian dancer and choreographer who created a fusion style blending European theatrical/stage techniques (lighting, stagecraft, group choreography) with Indian classical and folk dance forms. (उदय शंकर — भारतीय नृत्य के अग्रदूत)

 

• He is widely regarded as the father of modern Indian dance and founded the Uday Shankar India Culture Centre at Almora, which trained many later stalwarts of Indian dance.

 

• He was the elder brother of the legendary sitarist Pandit Ravi Shankar, and his troupe toured extensively across Europe and America in the 1930s, popularising a distinctly modern, hybrid Indian dance idiom internationally.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Uday Shankar received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship, India's highest honour in the performing arts, and later the Padma Vibhushan (posthumously, 1971).

 

• His creative works include the ballet 'Kalpana' (1948), which remains a landmark in Indian dance-cinema.

 

NOTE

 

• Smita Nagdev (Option 1): A Kathak dancer, but not associated with this specific European-fusion pioneering style.

 

• Ravi Shankar (Option 2): A world-renowned sitar maestro (Uday Shankar's brother), not primarily known as a dancer/choreographer.

 

• Shovana Narayan (Option 3): A well-known contemporary Kathak exponent, not the pioneer of this East-West fusion dance style.

question:
Who among the following wrote the popular Telugu patriotic song 'Desamunu preminchumanna, manchi annadi

penchumanna' meaning 'Love the nation, grow the goodness'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gurajada Apparao.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gurajada Apparao, the eminent Telugu writer and social reformer, wrote the famous patriotic song 'Desamunu Preminchumanna...', part of his celebrated composition popularly known as 'Desa Bhakti Geetam'. (देश भक्ति गीत — गुराज़ादा अप्पाराव)

 

• The song extols true patriotism as working for the collective good and moral uplift of the nation ('love the nation, grow the goodness'), reflecting Gurajada's progressive, reformist vision of nationalism.

 

• Gurajada Apparao is best remembered as a pioneer of modern Telugu literature, notably for his path-breaking play 'Kanyasulkam', which critiqued social evils like child marriage and the dowry-like bride-price system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gurajada Apparao is credited with popularising spoken/colloquial Telugu (vyavaharika bhasha) in place of the older classical literary style, revolutionising Telugu prose and drama.

 

• The Andhra Pradesh government observes his birth anniversary (21 September) as 'Telugu Language Day' (Telugu Bhasha Dinotsavam).

 

NOTE

 

• Goparaju Ramachandra Rao (Option 1): Known as 'Gora', a noted rationalist and atheist social reformer, not the author of this song.

 

• Sri Krishnadevaraya (Option 3): The great Vijayanagara emperor and patron of Telugu literature (author of 'Amuktamalyada'), from an earlier era, not the writer of this modern patriotic song.

 

• Bammera Potana (Option 4): A 15th-century Telugu poet famed for translating the Bhagavata Purana into Telugu, unrelated to this composition.

question: Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education (LNIPE) is located at ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education (LNIPE) is located in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. (लक्ष्मीबाई राष्ट्रीय शारीरिक शिक्षा संस्थान — ग्वालियर, मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• Established in 1957, LNIPE is a Deemed-to-be-University and one of India's premier institutes for physical education, sports sciences and coaching.

 

• It is named after Rani Lakshmibai, the legendary queen of Jhansi and icon of the 1857 revolt, whose memorial/samadhi is also located in Gwalior.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• LNIPE offers undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes in Physical Education and Sports Sciences, and trains many national-level coaches and PE teachers.

 

• Gwalior is also home to other notable institutions like the Scindia School and the historic Gwalior Fort.

 

NOTE

 

• Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh (Options 2, 3 and 4): LNIPE is not located in these states; its campus is specifically in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.

question: Which of the following districts of India has the highest literacy rate as per Census 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Serchhip.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, Serchhip district in Mizoram recorded the highest literacy rate among all districts in India, at approximately 98.76%. (सर्वाधिक साक्षरता दर — सेरछिप, मिज़ोरम)

 

• Mizoram as a whole is one of India's most literate states, and several of its districts, including Serchhip and Aizawl, rank among the top nationally.

 

• The high literacy in Mizoram is often attributed to strong missionary-led educational institutions historically established in the region and sustained community emphasis on schooling.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala consistently ranks as India's most literate state overall (Census 2011: ~93.91%), with districts like Idukki and Ernakulam among its top performers, but individually they rank behind Serchhip nationally.

 

• India's national literacy rate as per Census 2011 was about 74.04%.

 

NOTE

 

• Champhai (Option 1): A district of Mizoram with a high literacy rate, but not the highest in the country as per Census 2011.

 

• Idukki (Option 3): A high-literacy district of Kerala, but ranked behind Serchhip nationally.

 

• Ernakulam (Option 4): Another high-literacy Kerala district, but again ranked behind Serchhip nationally.

question: How many countries participated in the first Asian Games held in 1951?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 11.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in 1951, with 11 countries participating. (प्रथम एशियाई खेल — नई दिल्ली, 1951)

 

• The Games featured around 489 athletes competing in 6 sporting disciplines, marking the birth of the modern Asian Games movement under the newly formed Asian Games Federation.

 

• India has hosted the Asian Games twice — in 1951 and again in 1982 (also at New Delhi).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Asian Games are held once every four years, organised by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA).

 

• The 2023 Asian Games were hosted by Hangzhou, China, while the 2026 edition is scheduled to be held in Nagoya, Japan.

 

NOTE

 

• 24, 16, 20 (Options 1, 3 and 4): These figures do not match the actual number of participating countries (11) at the inaugural 1951 Asian Games.

question: The Bist Doab Canal System and Makhu Canal System are associated with which state of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bist Doab Canal System and the Makhu Canal System are major irrigation canal networks located in Punjab. (बिस्त दोआब नहर प्रणाली — पंजाब)

 

• The Bist Doab region lies between the Beas and Sutlej rivers, and its canal system draws water to irrigate this fertile inter-riverine tract of Punjab.

 

• The Makhu Canal, drawing from the Sutlej river, similarly supports irrigation in the Punjab plains, which are part of India's most intensively irrigated agricultural belt.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Punjab's extensive canal irrigation network — including the historic Upper Bari Doab Canal and the Sirhind Canal — has been central to its status as a leading contributor to India's foodgrain production, especially during the Green Revolution.

 

• Punjab is characterised by the doab system of naming inter-river tracts, such as Bist Doab (Beas-Sutlej) and Bari Doab (Beas-Ravi).

 

NOTE

 

• Assam, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat (Options 2, 3 and 4): These states are not associated with the Bist Doab and Makhu canal systems, which are specific to Punjab's river geography.

question: On 9 August 2021, the Parliament had passed the Limited Liability Partnership (Amendment) Bill, 2021. It amended the:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Limited Liability Partnership (Amendment) Bill, 2021, passed by Parliament on 9 August 2021, amended the Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) Act, 2008. (सीमित दायित्व भागीदारी संशोधन विधेयक, 2021 — LLP अधिनियम 2008)

 

• The amendment aimed to decriminalise several minor procedural offences under the original Act (converting many penal provisions into civil defaults with monetary penalties), promoting ease of doing business.

 

• It also introduced the concept of 'Small LLPs' with lower compliance requirements and enabled the establishment of special courts for speedier trial of offences under the Act.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The original LLP Act, 2008, provided the legal framework for the Limited Liability Partnership business structure in India, combining features of a partnership and a company (limited liability with operational flexibility).

 

• LLPs are registered with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) and have become a popular structure for professional services firms and startups.

 

NOTE

 

• Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2012, 2004, 2016 (Options 1, 3 and 4): No such Acts exist by these years; the original governing statute that was amended in 2021 is the LLP Act, 2008.
